Wait x0 = fgpartition returns frozenset of objects, each object is frozenset of (value, (i,j)) cells. toindices converts to indices. So x1 is frozenset of frozensets of (i,j) indices.

Then mapply(vfrontier, x1): apply vfrontier to each element of x1. Each element is a frozenset of (i,j) indices. vfrontier takes a location IntegerTuple (i,j) and returns frozenset((i, location[1]) for i in range(30)). But here it's applied to a frozenset... apply(f, container) = type(container)(f(e) for e in container). So mapply(vfrontier, x1) iterates each index-set e in x1, applies vfrontier to e, and vfrontier expects a location tuple; e is a frozenset of tuples. Hmm.

Wait actually let's re-read: mapply(function, container) = merge(apply(function, container)). apply(function, container) = type(container)(function(e) for e in container). For x1 being frozenset of frozensets, apply(vfrontier, x1) = frozenset(vfrontier(e) for e in x1). vfrontier(e) where e is a frozenset... location[0], location[1] would fail unless e is a tuple.

Actually x1 = mapply(toindices, x0). x0 is a frozenset of objects (each object a frozenset of cells). mapply(toindices, x0) = merge(apply(toindices, x0)) = merge(frozenset(toindices(obj) for obj in x0)) = union of index sets = a single frozenset of all indices? merge flattens: merge(containers) = type(containers)(e for c in containers for e in c). So x1 = frozenset of all (i,j) indices of non-background cells.

Then x2 = mapply(vfrontier, x1): apply(vfrontier, x1) = frozenset(vfrontier(loc) for loc in x1). Each loc is (i,j) tuple. vfrontier returns frozenset((i', j) for i' in range(30)). x3 = underfill(I, 8, x2): fill 8 at indices in x2 that are background in I, within bounds.

So it fills the entire column (all rows) below/above? Actually vfrontier uses range(30) for all rows, then underfill restricts to grid bounds. So for every column that contains a non-background color, fill all background cells in that column with 8. But the description says "until you reach another colored square" - hmm, but underfill fills whole column's background cells. Actually since colored cells remain, and background cells in the column get 8. The description mentions lines from colored squares until reaching another colored square or end.
